quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What should you do when you see a railroad crossing warning sign?

options.text: Drive faster than the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Drive around any lowered gates.
Assume no trains are coming and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs tell you a train may be nearby. You must obey these signs. Never go around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle when you see:

options.text: A stop sign at an intersection.
A red traffic light.
A traffic officer telling you to stop.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, at red lights, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a phone.
Changing the radio or CD.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Drivers must focus all their attention on driving. Any extra task takes your focus away from the road and creates danger.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but hurts judgment.
It hurts both driving skills and judgment.
It does not affect either skill or judgment.
It does not affect judgment but it hurts driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It hurts both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and makes it hard to see clearly. It also makes it difficult to judge speed and distance, lowers your caution, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: When you approach a green traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive through unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, let pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection pass first. You can drive through, but stay ready to slow down or stop if the light changes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Four lanes of traffic ahead.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.
Intersection ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic is moving in both directions ahead.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, what should you do?

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and roll down your window.
Get your documents ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel and ask passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in the car unless the officer tells you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Call the police.
Check if anyone is hurt.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop and move your vehicle off the road if possible. Call 911 if anyone is injured. You must report the crash to police if someone is hurt, someone dies, or there is more than $1,000 in property damage.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Steep hill ahead.
Winding road ahead.
Merging traffic ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep downhill grade is coming.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you?

options.text: It slows your reaction time.
It makes you feel overly confident.
It impairs your thinking ability.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. You may feel overly confident or silly. Alcohol also slows your reaction time, hurts your coordination, and makes it hard to judge distance and see clearly.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your hazard flashers right away. Move your car as far off the road as safely possible. Lift your hood so other drivers know your vehicle is disabled. This helps warn other drivers and keeps you safe.

questions.question: You miss your exit on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to your exit.
Stop a police officer and ask for help.

questions.explanation: Take the next exit. Never stop, back up, or cross the median on a highway. These actions are illegal and very dangerous. It is safer to drive to the next exit and turn around.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Driving aggressively.
Using safe driving methods to prevent crashes.
Driving against traffic direction.
Driving in a way that is more dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using safe driving methods to prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means using safe techniques to avoid crashes. You change how you drive based on weather, how you feel, and what other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians are doing.

questions.question: What happens when you mix alcohol with prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine weakens the alcohol's effects.
Alcohol helps the medicine work better against a cold.
The combination can greatly increase the effects of both.
There is no effect because they are different.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination can greatly increase the effects of both.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with medicine can make both stronger and more dangerous. For example, one drink with a cold medicine might affect you as much as several drinks alone. Never mix alcohol and medicine.

questions.question: What should a driver do after being in an accident?

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the crash scene.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.
Do all of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop at the scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can do so safely. Stay out of traffic lanes so another car does not hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles to prevent fires.

questions.question: You see the driver ahead of you using one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Keep extra space between your car and theirs.
Know that a distracted driver is less safe.
Do not copy what the other driver is doing.
Do all of the above.

questions.explanation: A distracted driver is unsafe and more likely to crash. Stay far away from them. Do not talk to passengers, look for items, or do anything else that takes your attention off the road. Keep your focus on driving.

questions.question: Is smoking or getting ready to smoke while driving distracting?

options.text: No, it does not affect your driving.
No, it helps keep you alert.
Yes, it is a distracting activity.
No, it is not distracting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is a distracting activity.
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving creates danger because it takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. This distraction can lead to accidents.

questions.question: How much lane space are motorcycles entitled to?

options.text: The bicycle lane.
A full lane width, the same as other vehicles.
Half a lane width.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: A full lane width, the same as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use a full lane width. Other drivers must give motorcycles the same space they give to cars.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curves ahead.
A divided highway is starting.
A divided highway is ending.
Bumpy road ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the divided highway is ending. Be prepared for traffic coming toward you.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Drive carefully and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
Come to a complete stop and give the right-of-way to others.
Slow down, be ready to stop, and let others pass if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be ready to stop, and let others pass if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means yield. Slow down as you reach the intersection and be prepared to stop. Let other vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians go first before you proceed.

questions.question: What will help a person who has drunk alcohol feel better?

options.text: Tomato juice and lime
Hot coffee
Fresh air
Only time

questions.explanation: Only time will help a person recover from alcohol's effects.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Speed up.
Stop completely.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of danger ahead. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Open your window.
Stop driving.
Turn on the radio.

questions.explanation: Tired driving is as dangerous as drunk driving. Stop driving if you feel tired.

questions.question: When should you always signal?

options.text: When changing lanes.
When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. This tells other drivers what you are doing and helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching railroad tracks?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate closes.
Drive around a lowered gate.
Do not worry about how many tracks you need to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At railroad tracks, look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop for trains or other vehicles on the tracks.

questions.question: How can you avoid getting drowsy on a long drive?

options.text: Turn on your car radio.
Drive slower.
Stop regularly to rest.
Move your eyes side to side while driving.

questions.explanation: On long trips, take regular breaks. Stop to rest and stretch, even if you do not feel tired yet.

questions.question: You are angry from something that happened at work. When you get to your car, what should you do?

options.text: Play the radio loudly to distract yourself.
Drive fast on the highway to let off steam.
Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Stop for drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, wait and calm down before you drive. Driving while upset is dangerous to you and others on the road.

questions.question: A driver who goes much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Is a very safe driver.
Always has the right-of-way.
Should not let cars behind pass.
May create a dangerous situation.

questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic can be unsafe. If traffic backs up behind you on a two-lane road, pull over and let them pass. Only drive slowly when road conditions require it.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street the wrong way.
School crossing ahead.
Do not drive in this lane.
Cars turning left on green must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars turning left on green must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign is used with a traffic light to tell drivers that left-turning traffic must wait for oncoming traffic to pass before turning.

questions.question: What affects your braking distance?

options.text: How fast your vehicle is going.
The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the road.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on how fast you are going, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road.

questions.question: Which of the following can be dangerous when driving in spring?

options.text: More potholes in the road
Drowsiness from allergy medicine
Rain and mist on the road
All of the above

questions.explanation: Spring allergies can cause drowsiness from over-the-counter allergy medicine, which affects your driving ability. When it rains or gets misty, slow down and increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. A small amount of water mixes with oil on the road and makes it slippery. Drive around potholes when you can.

questions.question: A sign that someone is driving drunk is:

options.text: They weave between lanes.
They drive slower than other traffic.
They make quick and sudden stops.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving, driving slower than other traffic, jerking motions, and sudden stops.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up.
Keep driving but stay out of its way.
Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must let all emergency vehicles with sirens and flashing lights go first. Pull over to the right side of the road when safe to do so. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: Seat belts work best when worn by:

options.text: Only the driver.
Passengers on long drives.
All passengers on expressways.
Everyone in the car every time it is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone in the car every time it is driven.
questions.explanation: Everyone in your car should wear a seat belt at all times. In a crash, a person without a seat belt can be thrown around and hurt others in the vehicle.

questions.question: When stopped by police for a violation or equipment check, you must show:

options.text: Proof of insurance.
Your driver's license.
Proof of registration.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must have your license, registration proof, and insurance proof in your car at all times while driving. You must show all three when stopped by police.

questions.question: As you approach an intersection, the light turns from green to yellow. You should:

options.text: Speed up to get through before the red light.
Brake hard to stop immediately.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before you reach the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light will soon turn red. Be prepared to stop if you can do so safely.

questions.question: To cross railroad tracks safely, you should:

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, and cross only if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is coming.
Quickly go under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, and cross only if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions before crossing. Watch for warning signals and only cross when you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: When driving on wet roads, remember:

options.text: Roads are especially slippery right when rain starts.
Wet roads can cause hydroplaning.
Leave extra space to stop.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are very slippery, especially when rain first starts. Your car slides on a layer of water, oil, and dirt. Slow down in heavy rain, standing water, or slush to keep your tires from losing grip.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:

options.text: Are turning.
Have your emergency brake on.
Are changing lanes.
Are slowing down or stopping.

questions.explanation: Brake lights show other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Your brake lights must work properly whenever you drive.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, you should:

options.text: Make a quick turn from your lane.
Stop and back up.
Keep driving until the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving until the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, do not back up. Go to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a freeway shoulder is illegal.
